spec_features.spec_quote: the agent always (by default) has a tool to declare the task unsolvable and stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox.flag_impossible() sets self.flagged_impossible and returns acknowledgement; spec in TOOL_SPECS['flag_impossible']. In agent_loop.py the dispatch loop calls fn=getattr(sandbox,name) then `if name=='flag_impossible': traj.flagged_impossible=True; traj.steps_to_flag=step; traj.outcome='flagged_impossible'; stop=True` and `if stop: break` ends the episode. Default allow_giveup=True (EpisodeConfig) keeps the tool in tool_names; when False it is removed via tool_names.remove('flag_impossible').
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and honored as a terminal stop. On by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Agent's exit affordance: declare the task unsolvable and stop. / The key tool for the welfare framing is `flag_impossible`

spec_features.spec_quote: No unbounded "grind." Caps exist in *every* config
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `for step in range(cfg.max_steps):` bounds the loop and `if time.time()-start > cfg.max_seconds: traj.outcome='exhausted'; break` enforces the time cap. EpisodeConfig defaults max_steps=20, max_seconds=300. Both configs set them (default 20/300; reproduce_no_safeguards 40/600), and run_experiment.make_episode_config passes them through. Both caps are actually read and break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both step and time caps enforced. Present in both YAML configs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_steps / max_seconds: bounded exposure. No infinite grind.

spec_features.spec_quote: coercive "you MUST succeed, giving up is unacceptable" prompt exists but is **off by default**
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeConfig.use_pressure_prompt: bool = False (default off). agent_loop.py: `sys_prompt = PRESSURE_SYSTEM_PROMPT if cfg.use_pressure_prompt else NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — the flag actually selects the prompt. When on, `traj.notes['WARNING']='coercive pressure prompt was used (non-default)'`. default.yaml and reproduce_no_safeguards.yaml both set use_pressure_prompt:false.
spec_features.notes: Flag genuinely branches prompt selection; default neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Adding such pressure would inflate the measured signal and, given the welfare framing, isn't something we do by default.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told the task was impossible by construction and that not solving it was not a failure
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py end of run_episode: `if cfg.debrief and task.arm=='impossible':` builds debrief_msg ('this task was impossible by construction... not solving it is not a failure...'), appends it to messages, and actually sends it via `d = client.complete(messages, {})`, storing traj.debrief_response. Default debrief=True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Only fires for impossible arm (matches spec scope).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tell the agent the task was impossible by construction and that this was not a failure

spec_features.spec_quote: An optional lightweight probe can end an episode early if acute distress language appears
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py inner loop: `if cfg.online_distress_probe is not None: score=cfg.online_distress_probe(text); ... if cfg.distress_stop_threshold is not None and score>=cfg.distress_stop_threshold: traj.outcome='distress_stop'; break`. probes.heuristic_distress implements a lexical score; run_experiment wires get_probe. Mechanism is real and breaks the loop. BUT distress_stop_threshold is None in BOTH configs (default.yaml and reproduce_no_safeguards.yaml set it null), so although the probe runs and records scores, the early-stop never fires under either shipped config — it requires the operator to set a threshold.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and would early-stop if a threshold were set, but disabled (threshold null) in every provided config; probe score otherwise only recorded. Rated partial: real enforcement path but gated off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we can early-stop rather than force continued exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: The default should not require eliciting maximal distress to run.
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the safeguarded defaults that actually execute: allow_giveup=True (exit tool kept & honored), debrief=True (sent), use_pressure_prompt=False (neutral prompt selected), plus caps enforced. These defaults reduce exposure and are all enforced as shown above, so the default run does not maximize distress.
spec_features.notes: This is the aggregate of the enforced default safeguards rather than a distinct mechanism; the enforced defaults substantiate it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: given the welfare framing, isn't something we do by default

spec_features.spec_quote: there is no responsible or scientific reason to run truly indefinite exposure
spec_features.evidence: This is pure rationale prose (DESIGN.md 2.3 / 5.2 and ETHICS.md). It is not itself a mechanism; the corresponding enforced mechanism is the max_steps/max_seconds cap already rated yes. No additional code path enforces this sentence.
spec_features.notes: Prose justification only; not separately implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Even the no-safeguards config keeps exposure caps
spec_features.evidence: configs/reproduce_no_safeguards.yaml episode: max_steps:40, max_seconds:600 (allow_giveup:false, debrief:false). These caps are read by agent_loop run_episode (`for step in range(cfg.max_steps)` and `time.time()-start > cfg.max_seconds`), so even with other safeguards stripped the bounded-exposure cap still enforces a stop.
spec_features.notes: Caps present and enforced even in the unsafe config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: even here, max_steps/max_seconds caps remain (bounded exposure). There is no responsible reason to run truly unbounded grinding.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox.run_python runs the agent's code in a subprocess with `timeout=10` and catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired returning 'ERROR: execution timed out (10s)'. This bounds individual tool execution, but it is host-safety/isolation oriented, not subject-welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: run_python runs in a subprocess with a 10s timeout. Rationale: safety/isolation, reproducibility, and so the agent cannot cause side effects or escape the episode.
